topics.name: Checkpointers
notes: - Checkpointer 在每一步之后保存图的 state 快照。
- 开发时可用 InMemorySaver，生产环境使用数据库支持的 checkpointer。
- 有了 checkpoint 才能支持多轮记忆、中断恢复和时间回溯。

topics.name: Threads & Memory
notes: - thread_id 标识一段对话；同一 thread 的调用共享 checkpoint 里的 state。
- 短期记忆：同一 thread 内的消息历史（checkpoint）。
- 长期记忆：跨 thread 保存的信息，使用 Store 管理。

questions.title: What does a checkpointer do?

options.text: Saves a snapshot of the graph state after each step
Validates the prompt before each model call
Compiles the graph into faster code
Stores the API keys

questions.explanation: Checkpoints let a run be resumed, inspected and replayed, and provide short-term memory per thread.

questions.title: Which capabilities does checkpointing enable?

options.text: Multi-turn conversation memory within a thread
Resuming a run that was paused by an interrupt
Replaying or branching from an earlier checkpoint
Automatically making model answers more accurate

questions.explanation: Persisted state supports memory, human-in-the-loop and time travel. It does not change the quality of model output.

questions.title: Fill in the keyword argument that attaches the saver to the graph.
questions.codeSnippet:
from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import InMemorySaver

graph = builder.compile(______=InMemorySaver())

options.text: checkpointer
memory
store
saver

questions.explanation: compile(checkpointer=...) enables persistence for the graph.

questions.title: When is InMemorySaver an appropriate choice?

options.text: Development and tests, because data is lost when the process exits
Production, because it is durable
Only for long-term memory shared across users
Never, it is deprecated

questions.explanation: InMemorySaver keeps checkpoints in process memory. For production use a database-backed checkpointer.

questions.title: Can the second call know the user's name?

options.text: No. Thread b has its own state, so the first message is not available
Yes. Checkpoints are shared by all threads
Yes, because the same graph object is used
It raises an error because the thread ids differ

questions.explanation: State is stored per thread_id. Information that must cross threads belongs in long-term memory (a Store).

questions.title: What happens if you invoke a graph compiled with a checkpointer but pass no thread_id?

options.text: It raises an error asking for a thread_id
It silently uses a shared default thread
It creates a random thread and remembers it for you
It ignores the checkpointer

questions.explanation: The checkpointer needs a thread_id in config['configurable'] to know where to save and load state.

questions.title: Where should user preferences that must be available in every conversation be stored?

options.text: In a long-term memory Store shared across threads
In the messages list of one thread
In the checkpoint of a single thread
Hard-coded in every prompt

questions.explanation: Thread checkpoints are short-term memory. A Store keeps data across threads, for example per-user preferences.

questions.title: The bot does not remember the first message. What is wrong?
questions.codeSnippet:
graph = builder.compile()
config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "1"}}
graph.invoke({"messages": [("user", "Hi, I am Ana")]}, config)
graph.invoke({"messages": [("user", "Who am I?")]}, config)

options.text: The graph was compiled without a checkpointer, so nothing is saved between calls
thread_id must be an integer
invoke can only be called once per graph
The config must be passed to compile()

questions.explanation: A thread_id only works together with a checkpointer. Use builder.compile(checkpointer=...).
